text:
### Observed differences

- **The order of two groups of activities is reversed.** In the earlier window, A35, A36 and A41 each ran in every trace at about 40% of the trace's length, A27 followed at about 46%, and A26 came later (about 60%) and led to A30 in about 99 in 100 of its outgoing transitions; A25 entered the group with its outgoing transitions split roughly equally across A35, A36 and A41 (about 38/31/27 in 100). In the later window, A25 leads to A27 in about 96 in 100 of its outgoing transitions, A26 runs earlier (about 53% of the trace) and now leads to A35, A36 and A41 (about 35/32/31 in 100) instead of to A30, while A35, A36 and A41 run later (about 58–59%) and now lead to A30 (about 30–34 in 100) instead of to A27. All six cross-group pairs reverse almost completely — for example A35 precedes A26 in about 99 in 100 earlier traces but follows it in about 98 in 100 later traces — while both members of each pair still occur together in every trace in both windows. [REL010, REL011, REL012, REL013, REL014, REL015, DIR005, DIR006, DIR007, DIR008, DIR009, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, POS006]

- **A02 now appears in far fewer traces.** In the earlier window it occurred in about 75 in 100 traces near the end of the trace (mean position about 0.93), A49 led to it in about 72 in 100 of A49's outgoing transitions, and it led to A50 in about 91 in 100 of its own. In the later window it occurs in only about 21 in 100 traces; A49 leads directly to A50 in about 83 in 100 of its outgoing transitions, A02's outgoing transitions are spread thinly over many targets (A50 only about 13 in 100), and in about 79 in 100 traces the partner activities (A25, A26, A27, A30, A35, A36, A41, A49, A50) occur without A02. When A02 does occur, it sits earlier and much more variably (mean about 0.55, spread more than twice as wide; based on 42 traces). [OCC001, DIR001, DIR011, POS001, REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006, REL007, REL008, REL009]

- **Smaller shifts.** A06 and A10 occur in more traces than before (from about 7 and 9 in 100 to about 19 and 22 in 100), though the earlier shares rest on only 13 and 17 traces; A47 leads to A48 somewhat less exclusively (about 81 in 100 of its outgoing transitions, down from about 97). [OCC002, OCC003, DIR010]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that, in the later window, the relative execution order of two groups of activities is reversed: A26 and A27, which previously ran after the group A35, A36, A41 (A27 directly after one of its members, A26 after the group and leading to A30), now run before it — A25 enters A27, A26 precedes the group, and the group now leads to A30. This is shown directly by the near-complete order reversal on all six cross-group activity pairs at unchanged 100% co-occurrence, and corroborated by the rerouted outgoing transitions of A25, A26, A35, A36 and A41 and by the opposite position shifts of the two groups. The 36 qualifying indicators, against roughly 0.6 expected if nothing had changed, cannot be explained by sampling noise as a whole. A competing explanation the evidence cannot rule out is that both windows contain a mixture of order variants whose proportions shifted rather than a single flow being reordered, although the near-deterministic flip (about 99 in 100 one way before, about 98 in 100 the other way after) makes a pure sampling artefact unlikely. [REL010, REL011, REL012, REL013, REL014, REL015, DIR005, DIR006, DIR007, DIR008, DIR009, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, POS006]

Other differences: A02 was executed in about 75 in 100 traces before and about 21 in 100 after, with A49 now leading directly to A50 in most cases instead of through A02 — consistent with A02 becoming skippable rather than removed, since it still occurs in a minority of traces, though its position when it occurs rests on 42 traces. A06 and A10 also participate more often (about 7 and 9 in 100 before versus about 19 and 22 after), on few earlier observations. [OCC001, DIR001, DIR011, POS001, REL001, REL008, OCC002, OCC003]
